latest.title: AWS-Native Observability on EKS Fargate: A Dual-Pipeline ADOT Architecture
latest.description:
EKS Fargate removes the operational burden of managing worker nodes. No node patching. No EC2 lifecycle management.

But it also removes the observability primitives most teams take for granted: you cannot run DaemonSets.

That single constraint forces a complete rethink of how you collect infrastructure telemetry. This post documents the architecture I implemented for a production microservice platform running on EKS Fargate — and the specific decisions that made it work.

latest.title: Decoding the "Brave" Truth: Building a British English Intent Analyzer with Claude 4.5 and AWS Step Functions
latest.description: This article explores building a high-context intent analyzer using AWS Step Functions and Claude 4.5. By routing requests via cultural flags, the author demonstrates how a deterministic workflow outperforms autonomous agents in cost-predictability and reliability. It highlights the technical advantages of a "Lambda-less" architecture using JSONata and direct SDK integration, offering a lean, scalable way to manage LLM orchestration while optimizing inference costs.

trending.title: AIdeas Finalist: ASET – Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth
trending.description:
ASET (Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth) is a scientific claim verification engine built  for the AI era — where information can be generated instantly, but trust cannot, to address the growing problem of hallucinated citations and  AI-generated information.

Instead of probabilistic prediction, ASET retrieves, analyzes, and synthesizes evidence from 1.2M+ indexed research papers to produce literature-backed verification reports for claims extracted from text, documents, webpages, images, and videos.
